newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening mixed to higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to higher on Wednesday as markets absorb the Federal Reserve's increase in interest rates, analysts said.
They pointed to strong rises in European markets as an indicator of Wall Street's performance. Those markets shrugged off the hike in federal funds rate and pushed higher.
"I think we will see a market on the plus side with a strong opening and maybe profit-taking late in the day," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Securities.
Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said, "I think we'll have a mixed opening as all the gurus weigh in (on the increase) ... and (then) it will be a fairly decent session."
She added that if the slumping technology sector "can get itself together that would be a good influence."
Cardillo said Wall Street now would be concerned with the another interest rate rise by the Fed.
"The question that is going to loom over the market for the next couple of weeks is when the next move will take place," he said.
They said February durable goods data out at 8030 EST/1330 GMT would have little effect on stock markets unless the figures were outside the range of expectations.
A consensus estimate by economists calls for a 0.4 percent drop in February durable goods against a rise of four percent in the previous period.
Excluding defense goods, the estimate calls for a drop of 0.6 percent against a rise of 5.2 percent in January.
Tokyo stocks ended mostly steady, with the Nikkei average up 32.84, or 0.18 percent, at 18,472.45. In London, the FTSE-100 index was up 45 at 4315.7.
U.S. stocks were mixed in London. AT&T Corp goes ex-dividend on Wednesday and its shares were down 1/4 at 35-3/4.
The dollar rose against the yen and was at 124.10/20 in Tokyo. The dollar was at 1.6912/22 against the mark in Europe.
The U.S. 30-year bond was up 5/32 to yield 6.95. The Standard & Poors 500 futures index was 2.10 at 797.30.

The New York Times Market Place column says the Fed rate rise will cause less bond speculation than a 1994 increase did since it is Japan's central bank that is doing the most recently to foster speculation.
Republic Industries Inc chairman Wayne Huizenga has enriched himself and his friends in ways that even some fans question, The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports.
